items.title: SAP Logistics Management: Direct Integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition – Part 1
items.author: abhijitbolakhe
items.text:
Overview : SAP LGM Integration with S/4Hana Cloud Private Edition 
 SAP Logistics Management (SAP LGM) is a comprehensive solution within the SAP ecosystem designed to orchestrate and optimize end-to-end logistics operations across the supply chain. It encompasses a broad set of functional capabilities — including warehouse management, transportation and carrier network, thus enabling organizations to manage the full flow of goods from inbound procurement through to outbound customer delivery. 
 It helps enterprises reduce operational costs, improve delivery accuracy, and respond swiftly to supply chain disruptions — making it a critical pillar for organizations pursuing digital transformation of their logistics and supply chain functions 

 Technically, SAP Logistics Management is a native cloud SaaS logistics solution on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP). 
 SAP LGM was introduced in early 2026 with integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, and further the Integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition has now been released. This ensures that the both the customers for our Public and Private Cloud can use the capabilities of SAP LGM for their logistics operations 
 Introduction 
 SAP Logistics Management can now talk to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition without any middleware in between. In the direct integration scenario, the two systems exchange SOAP messages and OData calls through the Cloud Connector alone, so you do not need an SAP Integration Suite tenant, integration flows, or iFlow monitoring for this connection. 
 This two-part blog series walks through the complete setup from end to end, in the order you would actually do it. Part 1 (this blog) covers the architecture, the prerequisites, preparing the S/4HANA system and exposing the inbound web services in SOA Manager. Part 2 covers the outbound web services, the Cloud Connector and the configuration in SAP Logistics Management. 
 It is written for Administrators, integration consultants and logistics functional consultants who are implementing SAP Logistics Management alongside an existing S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system. 
 Direct integration architecture 
 Direct integration connects SAP Logistics Management to S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition using SOAP-based web services through the Cloud Connector, with no middleware. It applies when SAP BTP can reach your S/4HANA system over a direct network connection, and this series covers that scenario only. 
 How the messages flow 
 The two directions take different paths, which is worth understanding before you start configuring. 
 S/4HANA to SAP Logistics Management: S/4HANA calls the SOAP endpoint of your SAP Logistics Management tenant over HTTPS. This carries warehouse requests such as outbound deliveries and stock transfer shipment advices. 
 SAP Logistics Management to S/4HANA: SAP Logistics Management calls back through a BTP destination and the Cloud Connector. This carries confirmations (shipping advice, stock transfer receipt) over SOAP and master data replication over OData. 

 Before you start 
 Prerequisites checklist 
 Your SAP BTP user has the Subaccount Administrator role collection in the SAP Logistics Management subaccount. 
 SAP Cloud Identity Services is set up and you have administrator authorization. 
 A business system exists in the S/4HANA system. 
 You have a Cloud Connector installed & Configured 
 Step 1: Prepare SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 
 Five preparation tasks come before any web service configuration: enable the OData services, define the warehouse, build the authorization role, create the technical user and activate the AIF content. 
 1.1 Define the warehouse 
 Define a SAP Logistics Management warehouse in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition by using below SAP Help Link 
 https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LOGISTICS_MANAGEMENT/ff6700aed66c43c48fe5351d55db2381/2042f82bbcb247af910693a562eecabf.html 

 1.2 Enable the OData services 
 SAP Logistics Management replicates business partners, products and purchase orders through OData, and posts changes back the same way. Both V2 and V4 services are involved. 

 Version 
 Services 
 Transaction 

 OData V2 
 API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV , API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV , 
 API_BUSINESS_PARTNER , API_BATCH_SRV 
 /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE 

 OData V4 
 API_PURCHASEORDER_2 , API_PRODUCT , CDI_CDS 
 /IWFND/V4_ADMIN 
 Enable the OData V2 Services: V2 services: 

 For the V4 service groups: 

 1.3 Create the PFCG role 
 One role carries the authorizations for all three interface types. In transaction PFCG , create a role (for example ZLGM_ROLE ) and add the services on the Menu tab as authorization defaults. 
 The four SOAP external services to enter are: 
 WAREHOUSESHIPPINGADVICE_IN/WAREHOUSE_SHIPPING_ADVICE_IN 
 WAREHOUSESHIPPINGADVICECANCELR/WAREHOUSE_SHIPPING_ADVICE_CANC 
 WAREHOUSESTOCKTRANSFERRECEIPT1/WAREHOUSE_STOCK_TRANSFER_RECEI 
 WAREHOUSESTOCKTRANSFERRECEIPTA/WAREHOUSE_STOCK_TRANSFER_RECEI 

 1.4 Create the technical user 
 This user is what the Cloud Connector destination and SAP Logistics Management use to log on to S/4HANA. (ZLGM_T_USER) 
 1.5 Enable AIF 
 Open transaction /AIF/CONTENT_EXTRACT . 
 Enter the development scenario ID SAP_AIF_0118 . 
 Choose Execute . 

 Step 2: Expose the inbound web services in S/4HANA 
 SAP Logistics Management confirms its warehouse activities by calling four SOAP services in S/4HANA. Each one needs its own service binding in SOA Manager, and each binding gives you an access URL that you enter later in SAP Logistics Management. 
 The service definitions are in package LE_IDW_SOA_SERVICES (transaction SE80 , under Enterprise Services > Service Definitions): 
 Open transaction SE80. Choose the package LE_IDW_SOA_SERVICES. Configure each service separately. Start with one service definition and repeat the process for each remaining service definition. 

 Service definition 
 Purpose 

 WarehouseShippingAdvice_In 
 Warehouse shipping advice 

 WarehouseShippingAdviceCancelR 
 Cancellation request for a warehouse shipping advice 

 WarehouseStockTransferReceiptA 
 Warehouse stock transfer receipt advice 

 WarehouseStockTransferReceipt1 
 Cancellation of a warehouse stock transfer receipt advice 
 Repeat this procedure for each of the four definitions : 

 What’s next 
 S/4HANA is now ready to exchange warehouse messages with SAP Logistics Management: the warehouse is defined, the OData services and the four inbound web services are exposed, and the technical user, authorization role and AIF content are in place. 
 In Part 2, we complete the integration: configuring the six outbound web services in SOA Manager, setting up the Cloud Connector and finishing the configuration in SAP Logistics Management, followed by a checklist to validate the setup end to end. 
 References 
 Technical Integration with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition: Direct Integration in the Integration Guide for SAP Logistics Management, SAP Help Portal.

items.title: Best Practices for Idempotency, Duplicate Payment Prevention and Transaction Persistence
items.author: AGA82
items.text:
Dear All, 
 We are designing an integration between an external business application and a bank's payment gateway using SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration). 
 The high-level integration flow is as follows: 

 A user initiates a payment from an external business application. 

 The application sends a payment initiation request to SAP Cloud Integration (CPI), including details such as Payment Request ID, Transaction Reference, Amount, Currency and Company Code. 

 CPI validates the request, generates a unique payment gateway order ID, prepares the required encrypted request and returns the payment initiation details to the external application. 

 The user's browser is redirected to the bank's hosted payment page to complete the payment. 

 The payment gateway sends the payment response and a separate webhook notification to CPI. 

 CPI verifies the transaction status, using the payment gateway's transaction inquiry API when required, and updates the payment status in the external application. 
 The key requirement is to prevent duplicate payment processing and maintain reliable transaction tracking throughout the payment lifecycle. 
 Consider the following scenarios: 

 The external application sends the same payment initiation request multiple times because of a network timeout or retry. 

 CPI processes the request, but its response to the external application is lost. The application subsequently retries the same request. 

 Two identical payment requests arrive concurrently in CPI. 

 The payment gateway successfully processes a payment, but CPI does not receive the response or webhook notification. 

 CPI receives the same webhook notification multiple times. 

 The payment is successful at the gateway, but CPI fails to update the payment status in the external application. 
 We are considering using the Payment Request ID received from the external application as an idempotency key and maintaining transaction details in a persistent store. 
 I would appreciate the community's recommendations on the following: 

 What is the recommended approach to implement idempotency and prevent duplicate payment processing in SAP Cloud Integration? 

 What persistence options are suitable for maintaining payment transaction details? For example, CPI Data Store, or other options. 

 Is CPI Data Store suitable for this use case, considering concurrent requests, duplicate checks, transaction updates and retrieval across multiple iFlows? 

 How can we ensure atomicity when checking and creating a payment request record? A simple Data Store Get followed by Write may not prevent two concurrent requests from processing the same Payment Request ID. 

 What is the recommended approach to maintain payment status across separate iFlows handling payment initiation, gateway callbacks, webhooks, transaction inquiries and application status updates? 

 How should uncertain payment outcomes be handled, particularly when the payment gateway has processed the payment but CPI has not received the response? How can we prevent a second payment from being initiated before verifying the original transaction? 

 What are the recommended practices for transaction retention, reconciliation, monitoring and recovery? 
 I am particularly interested in practical implementation experiences and recommended architectural patterns for handling financial transactions in SAP Integration Suite. 
 Thanks in advance for your suggestions.

33.summary: A vendor blog announcing the Usage Records OData V4 API (v2), available from October 27, 2026. It says v1 (RESTful, proprietary query syntax) was deprecated on November 9, 2026 and will be decommissioned on November 9, 2027. The post covers the v2 query options ($select, $expand, $filter, $count, $orderby, $top), lambda any() filtering, the standard OData V4 $batch format, a field rename table, and migration examples for create/upsert, discard, delete and list. The migration section is cut off mid-way at the pagination part.
key_points: Base URL changes from /v1 to /v2; OAuth scopes are stated to be unchanged.
Five field renames: userTechnicalId to technicalResourceId, isAssigned to assigned, changedAt to modifiedAt, changedBy to modifiedBy, subscriptionNumber to subscriptionDocumentNumber.
Single upsert moves from POST /usage-records to POST /UsageRecords/upsertByLogicalKey with the payload wrapped in a 'value' object.
Lambda filter example: $filter=customReferences/any(c:c/typeCode eq 'SYSTEM_TYPE').
Total count moves from the x-count header into the body as @count when $count=true is used.
$batch now uses standard multipart/mixed and supports upsert, discard, delete and retrieve; a changeset gives atomic all-or-nothing behaviour and is optional.
technical_details: GET /UsageRecords?$select=...&$expand=items($select=itemNumber;$expand=fields($select=fieldCode,stringValue))
$filter=contains(metricId,'CALL'), startswith(technicalResourceId,'device-'), metricId in (...)
POST /UsageRecords/upsertByLogicalKey with JSON body {"value": {...}}
POST /UsageRecords({id})/discard and DELETE /UsageRecords({id})
Batch: Content-Type multipart/mixed; boundary=batch_..., nested changeset with Content-ID per request
v1 list params filter=, sort=, pageSize=, pageNumber= become $filter=, $orderby=, $top= in v2
Dates: v2 available 27 Oct 2026; v1 deprecated 9 Nov 2026; v1 decommissioned 9 Nov 2027
33.why_it_matters: Anyone integrating with Usage Records has a hard deadline (decommission 9 Nov 2027). The field renames and the upsert endpoint change would break existing code silently if not caught, so this is a concrete migration checklist.
33.teaching_angle: Use it as a worked example of moving from a proprietary REST query syntax to OData V4 query options and multipart batch. Have students write the v1-to-v2 mapping for one endpoint, then explain why the changeset is atomic and why upsertByLogicalKey needs a stable logical key.

111.summary: A discussion post asking for architecture advice on preventing duplicate payments when a payment gateway is integrated through SAP Cloud Integration. It sets out a six-step flow (initiation, redirect to hosted page, gateway response and webhook, inquiry API, status update) and six failure scenarios, including retries, lost responses, concurrent identical requests and duplicate webhooks. The author proposes the Payment Request ID as an idempotency key with a persistent store, and asks whether CPI Data Store is adequate. No answers are included in the post.
key_points: Proposed idempotency key: the Payment Request ID from the calling application.
Concern raised: a Data Store Get followed by a Write is not atomic, so two concurrent requests can both pass the duplicate check.
Open questions on whether CPI Data Store fits concurrent checks, status updates and cross-iFlow retrieval.
Uncertain outcomes (gateway paid, CPI got no response) need an inquiry-before-retry policy.
Asks about reconciliation, retention, monitoring and recovery for financial transactions.
technical_details: CPI iFlows: payment initiation, gateway callback, webhook receiver, transaction inquiry, status update to the external app
CPI Data Store (Get/Write/Select/Delete operations) named as the candidate persistence layer
Inputs: Payment Request ID, Transaction Reference, Amount, Currency, Company Code
Gateway transaction inquiry API used to verify uncertain outcomes
No specific SAP notes, versions or code are given
111.why_it_matters: Duplicate payment prevention is a real design problem for CPI, and the atomicity gap in a naive Get-then-Write check is the central technical point. The thread is a good place to test whether CPI can give the guarantees needed or whether an external transactional store is required.
111.developer_problem: How to guarantee idempotent, duplicate-free payment initiation and status tracking across several CPI iFlows when requests can be retried, arrive concurrently or be duplicated by webhooks.
111.teaching_angle: Use this as an interview case. Ask candidates to design an atomic idempotency check. A good answer covers a unique-key insert in an external DB (or a single-writer queue) instead of Get-then-Write, a state machine (INITIATED, PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED), inquiry before any retry, and idempotent webhook handling. Make clear that CPI Data Store is not a transactional database and that its concurrency guarantees should be checked in documentation rather than assumed.

98.why_it_matters: Shows a middleware-free integration pattern that S/4HANA Private Edition consultants will need to set up. The list of services and the authorization approach give a concrete starting point for the setup.
98.teaching_angle: Good for teaching the difference between SOAP inbound services (SOA Manager) and OData service activation (IWFND). Ask students to trace which system calls which and where each credential is used, then compare this with a CPI-based design.

The poster asks for the standard way to cover all PR creation channels and whether to validate on the source object and raise SWE_EVENT_CREATE_IN_UPD_TASK for BUS2105 by hand. The post has no answer and no code.
key_points: Validation and Flexible Workflow work for interactive PRs (ME51N/ME52N/Fiori) but not for PRs generated from PM orders or SD sales orders.
The poster asks whether one standard MM BAdI covers all PR creation channels or whether validation must be placed on the source side.
The poster proposes raising SWE_EVENT_CREATE_IN_UPD_TASK for BUS2105 manually, which mixes a workflow event with a validation hook.

digest.headline: A quiet day of mostly unanswered community questions: BAdI call-path problems, a silent BAPI no-op, and one OData v1-to-v2 migration with a hard deadline.
digest.overview:
Today's material is mostly community questions with no answers. The ABAP-relevant ones share a pattern: a hook (BAdI, substitution exit, BAPI) does not behave the way the developer assumed. Examples are PR validation that does not fire for PM and SD generated requisitions, a batch classification BAdI that does not fire after production goods receipt, and BAPI_PO_CHANGE returning success without changing the address. The only release-style item is a migration guide for the Usage Records API, from v1 to OData V4 v2.

For a trainer, the common point is verification. Trace the real call path per channel, read back the data after a BAPI, and check which framework owns a field before writing code. None of the posts contain confirmed fixes, so treat the suggested directions as hypotheses to test in a system.

top_stories.title: PR validation and Flexible Workflow do not fire for PRs created from PM and SD orders
top_stories.summary: A custom PR validation (ME_PROCESS_REQ_CUST / MM_PUR_S4_PR_CHECK) and a Flexible Workflow work for ME51N, ME52N and Fiori, but not when the PR is generated from PM maintenance orders (IW31/IW32) or SD sales orders (VA01/VA02). The poster asks for one standard hook that covers all channels and considers raising BUS2105 events manually. The question appears three times, with no answer.
top_stories.why_it_matters: A check placed in the UI-facing BAdI is easily assumed to cover every creation path. Verify each channel with a breakpoint and a call-stack check. A manually raised workflow event is not a substitute for validation.

top_stories.title: BAPI_PO_CHANGE reports success but does not change the delivery address
top_stories.summary: When EKPO-ADRNR is blank, the BAPI returns an empty RETURN table and the delivery address is not persisted. With ADRNR filled, the same call works. The post does not show the address structures passed, or whether a commit is called.
top_stories.why_it_matters: A silent no-op in a change BAPI is dangerous in an approval process. Always inspect RETURN, commit, and read the object back. The root cause is not given in the post.

top_stories.title: Batch classification after production GR: BAdI MMIM_GR4XY_PROVIDE_DATA does not fire
top_stories.summary: The poster needs PROCESSED_TARIFF and PROCESSED_CAN_SURTAX calculated on output batches from the final batch weight, after batch creation and all production goods movements. The chosen BAdI is not triggered. The question is posted three times (refs 71, 73, 83), with no answer.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The case shows that a BAdI name found by search does not guarantee it runs for a given goods movement path, and that timing requirements need a call-stack trace.

top_stories.title: Usage Records OData API v2: v1 decommission on 9 Nov 2027
top_stories.summary: The v2 API (OData V4) has been available since 27 Oct 2026. v1 is deprecated and will be decommissioned on 9 Nov 2027. Changes include five field renames, upsertByLogicalKey with a value wrapper, $count moved from a header into the body as @count, and standard multipart/mixed $batch with optional atomic changesets.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The renames and the changed upsert endpoint will break existing integrations if they are not caught. The post gives a concrete migration checklist, though the pagination section is cut off.

top_stories.title: Idempotent payment initiation through CPI
top_stories.summary: A design question on preventing duplicate payments across several CPI iFlows. The key point is that Data Store Get followed by Write is not atomic, so concurrent requests can both pass the duplicate check. The post proposes the Payment Request ID as the idempotency key. No answers are given.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The atomicity gap is the central design issue. The post does not say whether CPI offers a guarantee, so check documentation and consider a unique-key store outside CPI.

deep_dives.title: Tracing which creation channels call your BAdI (PR validation case)
deep_dives.explanation:
The posts about PR validation describe a BAdI (`ME_PROCESS_REQ_CUST` / `MM_PUR_S4_PR_CHECK`) that fires for ME51N, ME52N and Fiori, but not for PRs generated from PM or SD orders. The posts do not give a cause, so what follows is a method, not a confirmed answer.

Start by listing every channel that creates a PR: interactive UI, PM order components, SD-generated requisitions, and any BAPI or background job. For each channel, set an external breakpoint in the BAdI method (or in the call site of the BAdI) and run the scenario. If the breakpoint is not reached, look at the call stack from the source document to see which API creates the requisition. That API decides which hooks are available.

Keep two concerns apart. Validation must run before the document is saved and be able to reject it. A workflow event, such as a manually raised event for BUS2105 via `SWE_EVENT_CREATE_IN_UPD_TASK`, only starts a process after the fact. It cannot replace a check. If a single MM-level hook does not cover a channel, the options are to place the check on the source object side or to check again at a later stage. Weigh these against duplication of logic and the risk of missing a path.

For class use, give students the same scenario in a sandbox and ask them to produce a table: channel, API called, hooks reached, where the check should live.
key_concepts: BAdI call path vs creation channel

deep_dives.title: Verifying change BAPIs: BAPI_PO_CHANGE returning success with no effect
deep_dives.explanation:
The poster reports `BAPI_PO_CHANGE` returning an empty `RETURN` table while the delivery address does not change, but only when `EKPO-ADRNR` is blank. The post does not show the parameters, so the cause is not established. The point to teach is how to verify a change BAPI.

A robust pattern: fill both the data structure and its corresponding X-structure with the right item key and flags, call the BAPI, then loop over `RETURN` for types E, A and also W. An empty `RETURN` is not proof of success. Then call `BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT` with `WAIT = abap_true` on success, or `BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK` otherwise. Finally read the PO back (`BAPI_PO_GETDETAIL` or a select on EKPO and the address data) and compare to the intended value.

For a blank address number, a plausible hypothesis is that the BAPI has no existing address record to update and so needs a different input for creating one. Treat this as something to test in a system, not as a known fact. Compare the BAPI's behaviour with ME22N for the same PO, and check the BAPI documentation and SAP notes.

In a controlled approval process, the read-back check should be part of the program, so that a silent no-op raises an error instead of marking the change as done.

deep_dives.title: Moving from a proprietary REST API to OData V4: the Usage Records v2 checklist
deep_dives.explanation:
The Usage Records v2 migration is a compact example of what changes when a proprietary REST API becomes OData V4. List parameters `filter`, `sort`, `pageSize` and `pageNumber` become `$filter`, `$orderby` and `$top`. The total count moves from the `x-count` header into the body as `@count` when `$count=true` is used. Collection filters use lambda operators such as `customReferences/any(c:c/typeCode eq 'SYSTEM_TYPE')`.

Breaking changes need a field-level map: userTechnicalId to technicalResourceId, isAssigned to assigned, changedAt to modifiedAt, changedBy to modifiedBy, subscriptionNumber to subscriptionDocumentNumber. Single upsert changes from `POST /usage-records` to `POST /UsageRecords/upsertByLogicalKey` with the payload wrapped in a `value` object. A client that ignores the renames will not necessarily fail loudly, so contract tests against v2 are advisable.

Batch now uses standard multipart/mixed. A changeset gives all-or-nothing behaviour and is optional, so requests outside a changeset are processed independently. The same concepts apply to RAP-based OData V4 services you build in ABAP, so this is a useful reference for what consumers expect. The source post stops before the pagination section, so check the full documentation there.

*Empty RETURN does not mean the BAPI worked.*

A community post today: BAPI_PO_CHANGE returns no messages, but the delivery address is not saved when EKPO-ADRNR is blank. It works when ADRNR is filled.

The cause is not confirmed in the post. The checks are still standard:
1. Check RETURN for E, A and W
2. Fill the X-structures
3. BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT with WAIT
4. Read the PO back and compare

In an approval process, step 4 should be in the code, not only in testing.

post_drafts.title: Does your PR check cover every channel?
post_drafts.text:
*Your BAdI may only cover the UI.*

A poster has PR validation (ME_PROCESS_REQ_CUST / MM_PUR_S4_PR_CHECK) and a Flexible Workflow. Both work in ME51N, ME52N and Fiori.

Neither runs when the PR is generated from a PM order or an SD sales order.

*Takeaway:* list every way a document can be created, and put a breakpoint in each path. Don't assume one hook sees all of them.

Also, a manually raised workflow event is not validation.

interview_questions.question: A custom PR validation BAdI works in ME51N and Fiori but not for PRs generated from PM orders. How do you investigate and decide where the check belongs?
interview_questions.answer: First I list every channel that creates a PR: interactive UI, PM order components, SD-generated requisitions, and any BAPI or batch. For each one I set an external breakpoint in the BAdI method and run the scenario. Where it is not reached, I read the call stack from the source document to find which API creates the PR, because that API determines which hooks exist. I then separate validation from workflow: a check must run before save and be able to reject the document, while an event such as one raised for BUS2105 only starts a process afterwards. If no MM-level hook covers a channel, I place the check on the source object side or at a later stage, and accept the cost of keeping logic in two places. I document the channel-to-hook mapping so new channels are tested.

interview_questions.question: BAPI_PO_CHANGE returns an empty RETURN table, but the delivery address is not changed. How do you make such a call reliable?
interview_questions.answer: An empty RETURN is not proof of success. I make sure the data structure and its X-structure are both filled with the correct item key, and I evaluate RETURN for types E, A and W. On success I call BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT with WAIT = abap_true, otherwise BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK. Then I read the PO back, for example with BAPI_PO_GETDETAIL, and compare the address with the intended value, raising an error if they differ. For the reported case with blank EKPO-ADRNR, the post does not give the cause, so I would compare with ME22N for the same PO and check SAP notes and BAPI documentation. In an approval process the read-back check belongs in the program itself.

interview_questions.question: How would you design an idempotent payment initiation across several CPI iFlows, given that a Data Store Get followed by Write is not atomic?
interview_questions.answer: The duplicate check must be a single atomic operation, not a read followed by a write. I would use a store with a unique constraint on the Payment Request ID, where the insert itself is the check, so one of two concurrent requests fails. A single-writer queue is an alternative. I would keep an explicit state machine such as INITIATED, PENDING, SUCCESS and FAILED, and persist the state before calling the gateway. For uncertain outcomes, such as the gateway charging but CPI missing the response, I call the gateway inquiry API before any retry. Webhooks are handled idempotently by keying on the transaction reference and ignoring state transitions already applied. I would not assume CPI Data Store gives transactional concurrency guarantees without confirming this in the documentation, and I would add reconciliation, retention and monitoring.
